title: Numerical methods, stability and error contracts
outcome: Compare explicit numerical approximations with known solutions and distinguish stability, positivity, residuals and position error.

exercises.title: Refine the time step
exercises.task: Compare Euler with 4 and 20 steps for rate 1.
exercises.expected: The fine final value is closer to exp(-1).
exercises.hint: Use the analytic solution as an independent reference.
exercises.answer: This checks the stated smooth problem and does not imply that every refinement improves every numerical task.

exercises.title: Inspect the complete path
exercises.expected: The path includes a negative intermediate value.
exercises.hint: Stability and positivity have different requirements.
exercises.answer: A positive final value alone can hide an unphysical intermediate state.

exercises.title: Require a root bracket
exercises.expected: The helper rejects the absent sign change.
exercises.hint: The bracketing invariant must hold before iteration.
exercises.answer: A numerical routine cannot create a real root where the stated evidence does not support one.

exercises.title: Bound the iteration budget
exercises.task: Allow only one bisection iteration for square-root 2.
exercises.hint: Do not label the last iterate converged automatically.
exercises.answer: A stopped computation needs a clear termination reason and evidence about its remaining error.

exercises.title: Compare quadrature resolution
exercises.task: Integrate x squared using the two trapezoidal grids.
exercises.expected: The refined approximation is closer to 1/3.
exercises.hint: Keep the function and interval unchanged.
exercises.answer: A known integral helps separate discretization error from implementation errors.

exercises.title: Name tolerance units
exercises.task: Compare a root-position tolerance with a function residual.
exercises.expected: They have different units and meanings.
exercises.hint: The derivative scale connects them only under additional conditions.
exercises.answer: A small residual alone does not always imply a small position error in an ill-conditioned problem.
